The laws of logarithms are:

- ${log}_{n}⁡(a)+{log}_{n}⁡(b)={log}_{n}⁡(ab)$ - the product rule

- ${log}_{n}⁡(a)-{log}_{n}⁡(b)={log}_{n}⁡(\frac{a}{b})$ - the quotient rule

- ${log}_{n}⁡({c}^{m})=m{log}_{n}⁡(c)$ - the power rule

Using the quotient rule for logarithms, we get

$$
{log}_{2}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{x}{y}^{2}}{z})={log}_{2}⁡(\sqrt{x}{y}^{2})-{log}_{2}⁡(z).
$$

Now, using the product rule for logarithms, we obtain

$$
{log}_{2}⁡(\sqrt{x}{y}^{2})-{log}_{2}⁡(z)={log}_{2}⁡(\sqrt{x})+{log}_{2}⁡({y}^{2})-{log}_{2}⁡(z).
$$

Finally, using the power rule for logarithms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{2}⁡(\sqrt{x})+{log}_{2}⁡({y}^{2})-{log}_{2}⁡(z) & ={log}_{2}⁡({x}^{1/2})+{log}_{2}⁡({y}^{2})-{log}_{2}⁡(z) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)+2{log}_{2}⁡(y)-{log}_{2}⁡(z).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
{log}_{2}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{x}{y}^{2}}{z})=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)+2{log}_{2}⁡(y)-{log}_{2}⁡(z).
$$
